Hi Sofie / Lars —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Key points I captured:
- Primary compliance requirement: customer data for retail transactions must remain in EU (specifically SE/Sweden) at rest and in transit; non-sensitive telemetry may be routed for processing outside EU with logging.
- APAC support is a secondary requirement (Singapore) for a pilot in Q1; you prefer a single plan that can scale regionally or fall back gracefully.
- Latency SLO: sub-120ms 95th for auth/real-time risk checks; batch scoring can be higher.
- KMS/HSM: required for encryption at rest in the EU tenant.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Is NovaBank comfortable with hosted inference if model weights and token processing are pinned to an EU region and telemetry is scrubbed before any cross-region routing? Or do procurement/security teams require full private control (Private VPC or on-prem) for payment data fields?
2) Expected qps during pilot vs production (ballpark numbers) and percent of requests that include PII/payment tokens (affects cache isolation and routing policy).
3) For APAC pilot: is SSR (session state) allowed to replicate to SG, or must session keys remain EU-bound?

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send a short mutual action plan (attached) that maps requirements to recommended deployment options + pricing/lead time.
- Rishi (SE) will follow up with a region availability matrix and a preliminary latency model for EU-hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private on-prem.
- We can set a technical workshop with your infra team next week to walk through KMS and network requirements.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP requirements / decision table)

Thanks — available 10/22–10/24 for the technical workshop slots you suggested.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement and Security are open to Hosted if we get contractual guarantees that processing for payment-related requests never leaves the EU and keys are customer-managed (KMS). If there’s any chance of model inference crossing region boundaries for those requests, procurement will push for Private VPC.
- Pilot Q1 expected qps: ~80 peak, ~15% containing PII/payment tokens. Production target (12 months): 1.2k qps with bursts to 2k.
- For APAC pilot (SG): session state must be EU-persistent for payment flows; non-payment sessions can be routed to SG.

We’d like Rishi to confirm the technical feasibility of a hosting split: EU-isolated hosted endpoints for payment flows + SG-hosted endpoints for non-payment flows with a routing policy and audit logs.

Lars — can your team share any hard constraints on encryption key location?

Regards,

Thanks — adding technical notes and quick feasibility take below. Attaching a small region-availability-matrix (CSV) with which model families and capacity options are available in EU (Stockholm and Frankfurt) vs SG.

Quick feasibility notes:
- Hosted API (EU-only endpoints + customer-managed KMS): feasible if all PII/payment payloads are flagged client-side and routed to the EU-hosted endpoint. Redwood supports token-level routing policies and can enforce path-based routing at the ingress (we can supply SDK helpers). Audit logs are retained per-region and can be exported to your SIEM.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool in EU): gives predictable latency and tenant isolation for payment flows while allowing a separate Dedicated pool in SG for APAC non-payment traffic. This reduces cross-region hops entirely for sensitive flows.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full control over keys and networking; longer lead time (~8–12 weeks) and heavier operational commitment. Best if procurement will not accept any hosted guarantees.

Trade-offs to call out for your stakeholders:
- Latency: EU-hosted API should meet the 120ms SLO for 95th if traffic is single-region and models are quantized for the workload. Cross-region fallback (EU -> SG) will add ~50–120ms depending on path.
- Cost: Dedicated and Private are higher fixed-cost options but reduce egress/cross-region complexity.
- Compliance: Customer-managed KMS + per-region audit logs addresses many regulator asks; however, some auditors still require private tenancy for payment data—we should get a formal list of auditor requirements.

Next technical step I recommend: a 60-min workshop with your infra and security teams to walk through routing flags, SDK changes to tag sensitive payloads, and the KMS flow (we can bring diagrams).

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
